marks.gloss_en: בשלמא רצועה של תפילין -- כתיב וראו כל עמי הארץ כי שם ה' נקרא עליך, ותניא: ר' אליעזר הגדול אומר אלו תפילין שבראש
אלא חוט של תכלת מאי היא? -- the strap's merit is clear; what is the thread's?
R' Eliezer the Great: 'all the peoples of the earth shall see that the name of the Lord is called upon you' (Deut 28:10) -- these are the head-tefillin
דתניא, רבי מאיר אומר: מה נשתנה תכלת... דומה לכסא הכבוד
דתניא, רבי מאיר: תכלת דומה לים... לכסא הכבוד (= p_techelet_domeh_lakisse)
R' Meir: why is techelet singled out from all colours? techelet resembles the sea, the sea the sky, the sky sapphire, and sapphire the Throne of Glory (Ex 24:10; Ezek 1:26)
דכתיב ואת כל שללה תקבץ... ושרפת -- what lacks only gathering and burning
לא נצרכה אלא לעפר עפרה -- the ground's dust, which lacks detaching, is not included in 'gather and burn' (= p_afar_afara)
Ze'eiri: it is needed only for the dust of its dust [its ground]
ואמאי? איסורי הנאה הוא! -- the idolatrous city's dust is forbidden for benefit
R' Zeira: one may cover [the blood] with the dust of an idolatrous city
מצות לאו ליהנות ניתנו (= p_mitzvot_lav_lehanot)
Rava: mitzvot were not given for benefit
איתיביה רב רחומי לרבינא: שופר של עבודה זרה לא יתקע בו... לולב של עבודה זרה לא יטול -- מאי לאו אם תקע / נטל לא יצא?
a shofar of idolatry -- one may not blow it; a lulav of idolatry -- one may not take it
לא, אם תקע יצא... לא, אם נטל יצא -- the baraita forbids only ab initio
והתניא: תקע לא יצא, נטל לא יצא! -- an explicit baraita: he has not fulfilled
if he blew [an idolatrous shofar] he has not fulfilled; if he took [an idolatrous lulav] he has not fulfilled
in reward for Abraham's 'from a thread' (Gen 14:23), his children merited the thread of techelet
R' Abba: hard is eaten theft, for even the wholly righteous cannot return it
wherever you find the words of R' Eliezer son of R' Yose HaGelili in aggada, make your ear like a funnel
I gave greatness to Abraham -- he said 'I am dust and ashes'; to Moses and Aaron -- 'what are we'; to David -- 'I am a worm and no man'
but the nations are not so: given greatness, Nimrod, Pharaoh, Sennacherib, Nebuchadnezzar and Hiram king of Tyre exalted themselves
greater is what is said of Moses and Aaron than of Abraham: of Abraham 'I am dust and ashes', of Moses and Aaron 'and what are we'
R' Ila'a: the world endures only for one who restrains himself in a quarrel, as it says 'He hangs the earth on beli-mah'
R' Yitzchak on Ps 58:2: what is a man's craft in this world? to make himself like a mute
